fieldNotes.truckGate: Whole property is fully fenced (chain-link perimeter confirmed in multiple Street Views along Ray Klauck Way). Truck flow enters via an internal access road that wraps the NW/N of the plant down to the NE corner and into the secured drop yard. Controlled truck gate is near-certain for a fenced 1000-employee Nestlé plant of this scale, but the exact barrier arm could not be resolved in 2023 satellite/Street View.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No guard booth positively identified at the truck entrance in available imagery; a small structure exists near the NE corner but reads as a maintenance/utility shed, not a windowed guard booth beside the lane. Marked false with remoteGs true (kiosk/app check-in implied), low confidence.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Large dedicated drop yard on the SE/E of the plant packed with 80-110+ parked trailers in z19 imagery; clearly 50+.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Dock banks on the building's E and NE faces with trailers backed in; counted ~35-50 across faces, banded 25-50.
fieldNotes.railServed: Rail spur clearly runs into the property: tracks cross the yard pavement and curve in on the E side (z19 edocks/edrop crops). A UP main line also parallels the E boundary.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Two physically separate dock clusters on different building faces (E face and NE face) suggest split ship/receive; medium confidence.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge-of-town industrial park at the foot of the Wasatch range in Springville, a small city; per rubric tie-break, classified Rural.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Derived from perimeter box (~490m N-S x ~300m E-W) ~ 38 acres.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: Main plant plus two ancillary structures (small NE yard shed and a utility/process building cluster on the W).
